text_format_example:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

=== PATIENT INFORMATION ===
Age: 65
Sex: Male
Admission Date: 2024-01-15
Discharge Date: 2024-01-18

=== ENCOUNTER SUMMARY ===
Chief Complaint:
Chest pain and shortness of breath

History of Present Illness:
Patient presented with acute onset chest pain and dyspnea. EKG showed ST elevation. Cardiac enzymes elevated.

Hospital Course:
Patient was admitted to cardiac care unit. Underwent cardiac catheterization which showed 90% LAD stenosis. PCI performed with stent placement. Post-procedure course was uncomplicated.

=== DIAGNOSES ===
Primary Diagnosis:
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction

Secondary Diagnoses:
- Hypertension
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus

=== PROCEDURES AND TESTS ===
Procedures:
- Cardiac catheterization
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement

Imaging:
- EKG - ST elevation
- Cardiac catheterization - 90% LAD stenosis

Labs:
- Cardiac enzymes - elevated
- Troponin - elevated

=== MEDICATIONS ===
Discharge Medications:
1. Aspirin 81mg PO daily - Take with food to reduce stomach irritation
2. Clopidogrel 75mg PO daily - Take at same time each day
3. Atorvastatin 80mg PO daily - Take in evening
4. Metoprolol 25mg PO BID - Monitor heart rate and blood pressure
5. Lisinopril 10mg PO daily - Monitor for cough

Medication Changes:
- Added: Aspirin, Clopidogrel (dual antiplatelet therapy post-PCI)
- Continued: Metformin at same dose

=== ALLERGIES ===
No known drug allergies (NKDA)

=== VITALS AND KEY RESULTS ===
Last Vitals:
BP: 120/80, HR: 72, RR: 16, Temp: 98.6 F, O2 Sat: 98%

Key Results:
- EKG: Normal sinus rhythm, no acute changes
- Echocardiogram: EF 55%, no wall motion abnormalities
- Labs: All within normal limits

=== FOLLOW-UP AND INSTRUCTIONS ===
Follow-up Appointments:
- Cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks
- Primary care follow-up in 1 month

Return Precautions:
Return to ED immediately if:
- Chest pain or pressure
- Shortness of breath
- Dizziness or fainting
- Signs of bleeding (unusual bruising, blood in stool)

Patient Instructions:
Continue dual antiplatelet therapy as prescribed. Avoid heavy lifting for 1 week. Monitor incision site for signs of infection. Follow up with cardiology as scheduled.

=== DISPOSITION ===
Discharge Disposition:
Home with home health services

Condition on Discharge:
Stable

=== PROVIDERS AND SIGNOFF ===
Service Department: Cardiology
Author Role: Attending Physician
Signoff Date: 2024-01-18
